curriculum: The regular Dutch-taught part-time LLB is distinct from the Open Bachelor. The 2026–27 study guide year roster confirms 60 EC of introductory study, 80 EC of later compulsory courses, a 15 EC internal minor, 15 EC of open electives and the 10 EC final assignment. The 10 EC introductory criminal law course and ten 5 EC units account for the introductory phase. The 2026–27 guide separates introductory obligations and property law into distinct 5 EC components. The guide’s annual roster places Rechtswinkel first and the public-law essay first, which defines the choices illustrated here. Programme-page prose lists the minors in a different order, but does not designate a default; the ordered cohort roster is used for this illustration. The clinic is optional within the required internal-minor choice. The entrepreneur and public enforcement minors corroborate the two adjacent directions. The entrepreneur minor’s employment and social-security strand is corroborated by both sources; the two sources differ in naming its first commercial course, which is outside the selected example.
progression: Introductory law is recommended first and enrollment in it precedes registration for introductory EU law. Advanced contracts require enrollment in introductory obligations and property. Substantive criminal law requires completion of introductory criminal law, and Selected Topics in Criminal Law requires substantive criminal law and criminal procedure. The example plans leave room for a 12-month clinic after the 60 EC introductory phase, six specified 5 EC courses and one further eligible 5 EC course, for 95 EC. The 5 EC public-law essay and 5 EC advocacy practicum each require 140 earned EC and completion of or enrollment in their respective specified courses. Essay preparation requires both advanced administrative courses, both criminal law courses, EU law and International Law. The practicum requires contract, liability, property, civil procedure, both administrative and both criminal courses. The guide and model schedules keep the advanced compulsory work and finals in a compatible order; pace is flexible.
